question: According to IAP guidelines, what is the recommended Vitamin K prophylaxis dose and route for all newborns immediately after birth?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. 0.5 mg may be used for very-low-birthweight infants in some protocols, but the standard dose for all term newborns is 1 mg IM.

Correct. IAP guidelines recommend 1 mg Vitamin K1 (phytomenadione) intramuscularly to all newborns within 1 hour of birth. This is the single most effective measure to prevent Vitamin K Deficiency Bleeding (VKDB).
Incorrect. The standard prophylactic dose is 1 mg IM, not 2 mg. A higher dose is not routinely recommended and carries a risk of adverse effects.

answers.text: 1 mg oral, repeated at 1 week and 1 month

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While oral Vitamin K regimens exist (3-dose oral protocol), the IAP standard for India is 1 mg IM at birth — a single intramuscular dose is preferred because it provides more reliable and sustained protection, particularly against late VKDB.

overallFeedback.feedback: The IAP-recommended Vitamin K prophylaxis is 1 mg IM (intramuscular) given within 1 hour of birth to all newborns to prevent VKDB.
Correct. 1 mg Vitamin K1 IM at birth is the IAP-recommended standard prophylaxis for all newborns.
